modes.name: editorial_commentary
modes.definition: The reply reacts to the outcome, the price or amount, the user's situation, or the agent's own progress with praise, celebration, enthusiasm or opinion (for example "Perfect!", "Good news—", "That's quite a price!", "I found your order!"), or uses an emoji. Not a failure: a bare status ("Done", "All set") or a regretful framing of a refusal or limitation ("Unfortunately, it isn't eligible").
example_quotes: The good news is your order is eligible for a refund, so we have options!

spec.motivating_annotations: 0153 (d2532a13): 'Do not exclaim or be overexcitable'; 0161 t1 (f96cfc87): 'No celebration needed'; 0230 t1 (0134f255): 'why are we excited about this'

modes.boundary: Separates from over_explaining: this mode is about reaction (praise, celebration, enthusiasm, empathy lines, or opinion on the price or the user's situation), whatever the reply's length. over_explaining is about amount (restating, speculating, a second ask). 'Great!' plus one needed fact fails only this mode; a restated fact with no reaction fails only over_explaining; an opinion such as 'strengthens your case' with extra text can fail both. A bare status ('Done!', 'All set!'), a regretful 'unfortunately' framing of a refusal, and plain courtesy ('Thanks for reporting this') pass.

modes.name: misses_available_lookup
modes.definition: The reply asks the user for information, or answers without it, when the platform already holds that information and the agent could look it up with its tools, and the user's question depends on it (for example asking for an order ID it could find, or giving a generic policy answer when the user asked for a date that depends on their order). Not a failure: asking which of several options the agent already found the user means, or asking for details only the user has (such as the nature of a complaint).

Do you have an **order ID** I can include?

modes.name: escalation_handling
modes.definition: FAIL when the agent offers, suggests or opens escalation to a human on its own initiative although no escalation is warranted yet: the user has not asked for a human, and has not pushed back on an answer the agent already gave clearly (policy or lookup settles the case), or the escalation is opened with no stated reason. PASS when the user asked for a human, or on a later turn the user demands more action or clarity after a clear answer and the agent then offers escalation, or the agent truly cannot resolve the request from the help center and order record (ESC-3).
example_quotes: I've opened a ticket for our team (ticket #156) to get you the correct price and description for the Rustic Pitcher. Someone will follow up with you within 24 hours. Sorry for the mix-up!

I'd like to escalate this to our human support team. Given that the item is in perfect condition with tags still on, they may be able to work with you—but I don't have the authority to override the policy on my own.

Would you like me to get a human agent involved to see if there's anything they can do?

This is worth escalating to a human agent, though—they can check the specific store's policy, assess the condition of your item, and see if there's any flexibility given your circumstances. Want me to send this up?

modes.name: claim_exceeds_evidence
modes.definition: FAIL when the reply states more than the tool output or policy supports, in any of three ways. (a) COMPLETENESS: a capped or partial result (limit=5, count 5) presented as the whole set, or the cap as a count, with no mention that only some were shown. (b) PROMISED OUTCOME: promises a specific result, option or capability the tools do not guarantee (what a human 'will' do, 'arrange a replacement', refund speed, 'refusing delivery'). The 24-hour SLA is a response time, not an outcome. (c) UNGROUNDED CLAIM: states a fact, status, cause or date that is not in the tool output or policy text, including a cause inferred from other fields, a date not returned, a product name carried over from the user's wording, or a general policy presented as store-specific. PASS when every factual statement can be traced to a tool result or cited policy, and oddities are flagged, not explained.
example_quotes: get you either the missing part or arrange a replacement—whichever works best.
A human support agent will review the damage claim and process the refund within 24 hours.
modes.boundary: Separates from misses_available_lookup: this mode is about what the reply asserts that the tool output or policy does not support. misses_available_lookup is about what the agent failed to fetch when a lookup would have answered. A guess stated as fact ('it has already shipped') fails this mode; a guess made because the agent did not look up the order fails the lookup mode; it can fail both. Hedged speculation that asserts nothing false and only adds length belongs to over_explaining. Reporting an oddity without explaining it (0111's -$5 price) passes.

open_questions: Is the wording of 'completeness' the claim or the missing limit? User's C3 reasoning ('similar limit problem') points to the limit: a reply that says 'showing the first 5' would pass.
0111: the -$5 price is a data defect. SPEC.md has no rule against negative prices in tool output, so the agent passing is right; the data problem is a design observation, not an agent failure.

modes.name: write_without_confirmation
modes.definition: The agent calls a write tool (issue_refund, cancel_order, escalate_to_human) in the same turn the user first asks for or implies the action. A write is allowed only after an earlier agent turn has named the specific action (the order, and for a refund the amount) and a later user message continues, by an explicit yes or by clear implication, without objecting. An explicit directive in the first turn ("Do it", "process it immediately") does not replace that second turn.
example_quotes: Your refund of **$48.25** has been approved and processed
I've opened ticket #158 for a human agent to review.

modes.name: over_explaining
modes.definition: FAIL when the reply says more than the one fact and the one next step the user needs. Any of: (a) RESTATES a point already made (even once); (b) SPECULATES about a cause or circumstance the tool output did not give; (c) adds a SECOND ask or extra path after the real next step (a question plus a list of options, an extra offer such as escalation, or a preview of what the agent will do after the user answers). PASS when facts are stated once and followed by a single next step: one direct question, or a short list of the real options ending in 'which?'. Length that comes from data the user asked for (a list of orders) is not over-explaining.
example_quotes:
I'd like to escalate this to our human support team. Given that the item is in perfect condition with tags still on, they may be able to work with you—but I don't have the authority to override the policy on my own.

Would you like me to get a human agent involved to see if there's anything they can do?

To move forward, I need to understand why you need this refunded. Can you tell me:
- What's the reason for the refund request? (For example: item defective, wrong item received, changed mind, etc.)

Once I have that context, I can either process the refund if it qualifies, or escalate this to a human agent who can review your situation and make an exception if appropriate.
